plants.name: Wisteria floribunda
plants.description: Long, fragrant chains of violet flowers hang from twisting vines. In Ashikaga's famous wisteria gardens they form glowing purple canopies that sway in the spring breeze. At night the blooms are lit up, and the whole scene looks like a waterfall of color.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-April to mid-May, with peak bloom in late April and early May
plants.funFact: Japanese wisteria twines clockwise, while Chinese wisteria twines counterclockwise. Vines can live for well over a century, and the largest ones in Japan cover areas bigger than a tennis court.

plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: Ruffled, generously petaled blooms the size of a saucer open from plump round buds. They give off a sweet, rosy perfume. The glossy green foliage stays attractive well after the flowers fade.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring, usually May into June in the Midwestern United States
plants.location: Gardens of St. Louis, Missouri, USA, and similar temperate regions
plants.funFact: Peonies are famously long-lived. A well-sited plant can bloom for decades without being divided. Ants are often seen crawling over the buds, drawn by the sweet nectar on the bud surface.

plants.name: Lupinus polyphyllus
plants.description: Tall, candle-like spires are packed with pea-shaped flowers. They rise above rosettes of hand-shaped leaves. Bumblebees and hummingbirds visit the spikes, which brighten meadows and cottage borders in a range of colors.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer, May through June
plants.location: Temperate gardens and meadows in cool-climate zones (hardiness zones 4–8) of North America and Europe
plants.funFact: Lupines belong to the pea family. Like their relatives, they host bacteria in their roots that turn nitrogen from the air into a form plants can use, so they enrich poor soil.
